text:
GRU4Rec’s strongest established objectives are BPR-max and sampled cross-entropy. BPR-max concentrates learning on high-scoring negatives through softmax weighting and includes negative-score regularization; ordinary BPR can suffer vanishing gradients as negative counts increase. The official implementation recommends testing both objectives, typically with shared input/output embeddings; its practical guidance suggests roughly 2,048 additional negatives, fewer for small catalogs, and logQ=1 for cross-entropy only. These are starting points, not demonstrated Amazon HR@10 gains. [Official GRU4Rec](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec)

RecSys 2025’s “Correcting the LogQ Correction” identifies a subtle sampled-softmax issue: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined correction accounts for that distinction and reports improvements over standard logQ. Relevant to a single-GRU experiment, although its retrieval results do not establish gains for this benchmark. Correction must match the actual sampling distribution; hard-negative selection changes that distribution. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331)

Hard negatives may also be unobserved positives. UFNRec explicitly addresses this, but uses teacher/student supervision, making its full method unsuitable for the stipulated experiment. Practical hypothesis: compare regularized BPR-max against correctly implemented sampled softmax, using multiple negatives and masking accidental positives and observed training-history items. Test conservative hard-negative emphasis rather than assuming the highest-scoring unseen items are reliable negatives. These adaptations remain hypotheses; select by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, inspect Electronics separately, and preserve one GRU checkpoint per category. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116)
